project.name: integration-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contracts for the integration domain (V9 §18 / §91).
Members: OssPort (the storage port), UploadResponse (what an upload returns), CsdnBlogSyncPort, JuejinBlogSyncPort and BlogSyncResult.
OssPort and UploadResponse were reached for from four other future deployment units -- agent, knowledgebase, publishing and recitation all injected the concrete OssService and read its UploadResponse. After the split that is four services depending on another service's implementation class, so the port and its result type move to a module every side may depend on.
The two blog-sync ports come from the same judgement on a different capability. agent (dinqor-agent) and automation (dinqor-content-automation) both injected the concrete CsdnBlogSyncService / JuejinBlogSyncService that live in dinqor-platform-integration.
Deliberately two ports and not one port taking a platform string. Juejin's sync takes a category id and tag ids that CSDN has no concept of, so a merged port would either force the CSDN path to accept two parameters it never uses or drop a capability Juejin really has. Each port's method table is byte-for-byte its implementation's public surface, so the implementation just adds an "implements" clause -- there is no platform-dispatching adapter that could be wrong at runtime. The shared result shape is one record.
BlogSyncResult duplicates content-api's PublishResult on purpose: contracts must not depend on contracts (ADR-2), so each side carries an equivalent DTO and the conversion lives at the implementation boundary.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.integration.api, which sits inside the integration domain's own namespace because V9 §18 names the module integration-api. That is exactly the case SHARED_KERNEL had to be taught to express: its entries are now package prefixes matched longest-first, so this module is listed as integration.api rather than integration. Listing the bare domain would not misfile the domain -- it would make this contract invisible, because a business domain wins in the scanner and every type moved here would keep being counted as a domain edge. See the shared-kernel-classification gate and lib-extraction.md §6.1.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. OssPort deliberately takes byte[] and not Spring's MultipartFile: a contract is depended on by every service, including the WebFlux Gateway, so a Spring web type here would put spring-web on all of them and would also be the wrong shape for a call that has to survive becoming a network call. Callers holding a MultipartFile convert at the call site. The sync ports take java.util.List only, which is JDK.
UploadResponse is hand written rather than lombok annotated on purpose: this is a wire contract, so its shape should be readable without knowing lombok's defaults, and it is what lets the module stay JDK only without weakening the gate.
